newsitem.title: USA: WAL-MART COOPERATING IN HUDSON FOODS RECALL.
newsitem.headline: WAL-MART COOPERATING IN HUDSON FOODS RECALL.

text.p: BENTONVILLE, Ark., Aug. 13 - Wal-Mart Stores Inc said Wednesday it was cooperating fully with the U.S. Department of Agriculture in the voluntary recall by Hudson Foods Co of frozen ground beef patties.

The nation's biggest retailer said that its Wal-Mart Supercenters and Sam's Clubs are removing all Hudson frozen ground beef patties from their sales floors until each store and club has the opportunity to physically check every lot number to ensure that all affected product is destroyed.

On Tuesday, the USDA announced that Rogers, Ark.,-based Hudson Foods was recalling 20,000 pounds of frozen ground beef patties nationwide because the meat may be contaminated with the potentially deadly E.coli 0157:H7 bacteria.
Wal-Mart said its Supercenters carry a three-pound package of "Hudson Beef Burgers, Individually Quick Frozen" containing 12 four-ounce frozen patties.
The only product affected is marked with the code of 156A7 or 156B7, it said. However, customers may return any package of Hudson frozen patties for a full refund with no receipt required, it said.

It said its SAM'S Clubs carry 15 pound boxes of Hudson hamburgers containing 60 count four-ounce patties. The affected product is labeled with the code 155B7, it said. As in the Supercenters, SAM'S Clubs members may return any Hudson frozen hamburger pattie product to the club for a full refund with no receipt required.
